item.research_question: How does the composition of refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) based on Ti, Zr, Hf, V, and Nb affect their elastic properties, ideal tensile strength (ITS), and intrinsic ductility?
item.material_system: Four body-centered cubic (bcc) refractory HEAs: ZrNbHf, ZrTiNbHf, ZrVTiNb, and ZrVTiNbHf
item.processing_route: Ab initio alloy theory using the exact muffin-tin orbitals (EMTO) method combined with the coherent-potential approximation (CPA) within the local-density-approximation (LDA) exchange-correlation density functional; Brillouin zone integrations on a 27 × 27 × 27 k-points mesh
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tension along the [001] direction; quasi-static procedure with relaxation of unit cell lattice vectors perpendicular to [001] to allow symmetry lowering deformation
key_findings: The ITS of the ternary ZrNbHf alloy amounts to 2.64 GPa.
Adding equimolar Ti to ZrNbHf decreases the ITS to 2.28 GPa.
Adding both Ti and V to ZrNbHf enhances the ITS by nearly 42% compared to ZrNbHf.
Substituting Hf in ZrNbHf with equiatomic Ti and V increases the ITS by about 170%.
All investigated HEAs possess high elastic anisotropy with Zener anisotropy ratios indicating anisotropic behavior.
All HEAs show good extrinsic ductility with B/G ratios larger than 3.5 and positive Cauchy pressure.
The ZrVTiNb alloy exhibits an intrinsic brittle-to-ductile transition, failing via shear instability rather than cleavage.
The ITS correlates strongly with the fcc-bcc structural energy difference (SED) and average d-band occupation.
item.mechanism: The ideal tensile strength is determined by the ratio of group four elements to group five elements, which controls the average d-band filling; higher d-occupation leads to higher structural energy difference (SED) and consequently higher ITS, while specific d-band fillings (around 3.15) induce shear instabilities leading to intrinsic ductility.
item.limitations: The study is limited to ab initio predictions of ideal strength for defect-free crystals and does not account for extrinsic factors like dislocations, grain boundaries, or cracks that control strength in real materials.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that HEAs with d-band fillings larger than ~3.2 are expected to be intrinsically ductile and reach ITS values approaching those of group five elements as d-occupation approaches ~3.6.
quotes: The ITS of the ternary ZrNbHf alloy amounts to 2.64 GPa, and slightly decreases to 2.28 GPa by adding the fourth element Ti.
An even more pronounced impact of alloying on the ITS occurs if Hf in ZrNbHf is substituted with equiatomic Ti and V, which increases the ITS by about 170%.
The alloying effect on the ideal tensile strength of HEAs is explained by the d-band filling.
